- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 66.52–68.02), model overreacts with overshoots in the immediate following days.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, failing to capture mean reversion or rebound potential.
- Forecasts often underestimate the true mean of the 30-day history, especially when history is trending downward.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to recent high prices — fails to “follow” recent peaks unless they are very recent.
- In high-price environments (e.g., 75–80), model underestimates the true price by 5–10% on average, suggesting calibration drift.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in volatile periods — fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals.
- Model tends to “smooth” sharp declines, underestimating the depth of drops and overestimating recovery speed.
- In low-price environments (e.g., 60–65), model often overestimates the true price, suggesting a bias toward higher values when prices are falling.
